title: Batch B overlap plateaued at -15 after bounded replay and discovery fixes; next move requires a broader state-continuity system decision
symptom: Trusted, overlap-comparable Batch B reruns plateaued at overlap_verified_delta = -15 across campaigns b53cce73, a17d4492, b2bc709c, and f6ba985b. The previous placeholder/default contamination seam is no longer dominant, and bounded fixes for report-id family inference and misclassified numeric prereq slots passed locally and closed parts of the trace-level failure surface, but they produced no material overlap improvement. The latest traces show a deeper pattern: one target in a DLL family can still produce live runtime state, yet sibling targets later in the same package re-enter the same prerequisite chain and fail to reconstruct enough side-effect continuity after reinitialize. In workflow, WF_ConfirmWorkflow can still produce a live reservation/handle/nonce chain, while WF_GetReservationEcho, WF_GetWorkflowState, WF_CancelWorkflow, and WF_CommitShipment remain regressed. In reporting and pricing, later prereq chains still block or fail after earlier family producers succeed elsewhere in the same run. This means the current blocker is no longer just replay hygiene or slot repair; the missing capability is durable same-family state continuity across target boundaries under dense package context.
